featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience at Neptune Diagnostic and Fetal Medicine.
When I visited for a sonography at around 11:00 AM, the staff initially informed me that the total cost would be ₹5000. After that, I confirmed with my doctor and went back for the sonography after about half an hour. At that time, the staff suddenly told me that the total cost would be ₹6500. Later they said they had spoken with the accounts department and confirmed that I only needed to pay ₹5000, so I made the payment.
However, when I went the next day to collect my report, they again told me that the total amount was ₹6000 and asked me to pay an additional ₹1000. This information was given by a marketing staff member named Mukund. The details regarding the sonography and payment were earlier explained to me by staff member Vrunali and their account manager.
Apart from the billing confusion, the waiting time was extremely long and poorly managed. I went there at 11:00 AM, but at 3:30 PM they told me to come back in the evening at 6:30 PM. After returning in the evening, I was again made to wait for around 2 more hours. There seemed to be no respect for patients’ time.
For such a large organization, the time management and coordination are very poor. There was no senior person available, and the staff seemed to be working only based on guidance from each other, which created confusion.
Overall, I had a very bad service experience. *The doctor is very good and very cooperative* but the management and service system are very poor. Because of this experience, I will never visit this place again and will not recommend it to anyone.

I have the recording of the conversation about the charges and staff communication. If needed, I can provide it as proof. I will also share my experience on other review platforms so that other patients can be aware of the service quality.

Extremely disappointed and concerned about the reporting accuracy at this facility. I recently had a DEXA scan done here, and the center misclassified my biological sex as female on the official report.

Because DEXA scans evaluate bone density, T-scores, and health risk profiles based entirely on demographic baselines, a mistake like this completely invalidates the results. It skews the health interpretations and can easily lead to incorrect medical advice or missed risk factors.

When I brought this major discrepancy to the management's attention (handled by the manager, Tausif) to ask for a corrected report or a refund, the issue was not resolved satisfactorily. Since I am only in Mumbai temporarily, getting a rescan here isn't a viable option.

A diagnostic center's primary job is precision. If they cannot get basic demographic data right, you cannot trust the medical data they generate. Be incredibly careful and double-check every line of your reports if you choose to use this facility. I definitely won't be returning and highly recommend no one else to visit here.

Title: Disappointed with Lack of Discounts for Regular Blood Donations

Review:

I have been an active blood donor for several years, and I have participated in numerous blood donation camps organized by various organizations. While I appreciate the efforts made by ANVISHKA (GHATKOPAR WEST MUMBAI ) in collecting and distributing blood, I am deeply disappointed by the lack of recognition and benefits given to regular donors like myself.

Throughout the years, I have diligently donated my blood, always carrying my proof cards as evidence of my contributions. However, despite my consistent efforts, I have never received any discounts on blood when I required it during my own medical emergencies. I find this disheartening, as it seems that ANVISHKA does not value the loyalty and dedication of the blood donors

It is not unreasonable to expect some form of acknowledgment or incentive for those of us who selflessly give our blood to help others. Other blood banks and organizations often provide discounts or priority access to regular donors, recognizing their commitment and encouraging them to continue their vital contributions.

I sincerely hope that ANVISHKA takes this feedback into consideration and reevaluates their policies regarding discounts for regular blood donors. Acknowledging and rewarding the generosity of individuals who consistently support their cause would not only foster a stronger bond with the donor community but also motivate others to become regular blood donors.

I still believe in the importance of blood donation and will continue to contribute to the cause, but I hope ANVISHKA reconsiders their stance on recognizing the dedication of their regular donors.

What is a Hysterosalpingogram (HSG)?
Hysterosalpingogram (HSG) is a test that uses x-rays to examine both the uterine cavity and the fallopian tubes.
Why Fallopian Tubes Matter
The fallopian tubes are responsible capturing an egg after it is released from the ovary (ovulation), serving as a meeting point for sperm and eggs. Sperm fertilize the egg creating and embryo and the fallopian tube will transport the embryo towards the uterine cavity where the embryo will subsequently implant and develop.
The hysterosalpingogram, or HSG, will detect blockages in the fallopian tubes and abnormalities of the uterine cavity such as polyps, fibroids, and scar tissue that may prevent proper implantation and growth of the embryo. It will also detect congenital uterine malformations that result from incomplete or abnormal development of the uterus before birth.
Having a Hysterosalpingogram
The HSG is usually done in a radiology facility. After being greeted, you will be asked for a small urine sample to run a pregnancy test and to read and sign a consent form.
The best time to do the test is between the 5th and 12th day after the menstrual cycle started to avoid doing the test during menses or after the eggs is released (ovulation) thus avoiding doing the test during early pregnancy.
